structure.title: Inferno
structure.text: Dante descends through ordered punishments, hearing the dead explain themselves. Sympathy and moral classification repeatedly pull apart.

structure.title: Purgatorio and Paradiso
structure.text: The journey turns towards change, learning, and increasingly demanding forms of understanding. The landscape changes with what souls can become.

people.name: Beatrice
people.text: A figure connecting personal attachment with spiritual understanding.

context.title: Christian geography
context.text: Hell, purgatory, and heaven distinguish fixed estrangement, purification, and blessedness. Dante builds a poetic world around those differences.
context.takeaway: Each realm has a different relation to change.

context.title: Local quarrels
context.text: Many encounters concern Florentine politics and Dante's contemporaries. Brief notes help, but the speakers' wishes and evasions remain understandable without a complete political history.
context.takeaway: Start with what the speaker wants remembered.

notice.text: Compare punishment with the speaker's own account.
notice.why: Eloquence can make a morally compromised position attractive.
The person undergoing the journey does not begin with the poem's completed understanding.

opening: Lost in a dark wood, Dante finds that the way out leads through the dead. There he meets lovers, politicians, teachers, and enemies, each fixed in a condition that reveals what governed their lives. Some speak so beautifully that their punishment feels unbearable; others would prefer to keep their story off the record. Dante puts his own world on trial while travelling through it as a frightened, curious man who keeps discovering that sympathy and judgment do not reliably point in the same direction.
